you enjoy modding games to tailor the experience

cohorts.summary: Initial launch encounters severe character creation locks and setup barriers.

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering a soft lock during character creation where the game fails to progress past the name input screen.

citations.review_text: bought the special addition without the anniversary nor creation dlcs. I was enthused to see I still had access to the creation content, but less so when the game soft locks when you choose your name. It keeps looping to ask your name. After fully deleting all creation content, my deck still cannot pass the soft lock.
If planning to play on steam deck don’t bother, can’t get past name selection part of character creation. Tried all known work arounds including launch command and still absolutely nothing.
Installed it, watched the opening scene, got to the character creation and couldn’t get past it. It tells me to enter a name, then nothing. There is no excuse for a bug on something this basic.
unable to get passed character creation on steam deck

Played this on Xbox 360 at launch. Seeing it on sale thought I’d give it a go on steam deck. Thinking a 15 year old game must run well on this hand held by now. Wrong. Couldn’t even get past character creation, imputed a name and wouldn’t recognize to go forward. There’s some work arounds online sort of to get past it but come on, Bethesda doesn’t care enough to patch this simple problem so I don’t care enough to buy their products anymore. 
Also the fan was going already going hard just at the intro cutscene and character creation before even moving or playing. Thought to myself that’s a good omen not to put any time into it.

claims.claim: Game updates break installed mods, which frustrates players.

citations.review_text:
I'm sure this game is wonderful, but I'm leaving a bad review because of how uniquely bad the technical difficulties I had with this game were. I've had far better experiences running sketchy early-2000s shovelware in Window's compatibility mode, and that's a pretty low bar.

It hijacks my entire computer every time I launch it, it's an absolute struggle just to shut the game off, and there's always some oddly specific bug I have to Google up with another device to solve. 

Trying to mod the game wasn't easy for me either — but I did get it working eventually! Only for it all to break in an update. All those hours troubleshooting down the drain.

Kinda wish I got this on a console instead.

Another update broke all my mods.
Can't roll back to older version.
Getting real tired of this.

claims.claim: Combat mechanics are described as outdated, sloppy, or feeling broken without modifications.

citations.review_text: Good game. Combat is a little sloppy though.

Lately I've wanted to play this game cuz it seemed like playing an older rpg would be fun. Boy was I wrong. This game feels fundimentally broken without mods, as the combat breaks constantly and i get softlock bugs every 30 minutes. Not only that but my whole computers input system sometimes stops working and I have to restart it. This game is held together by mods that disable even being able to get achievements. And lacking the nostalgia I really don't see the point in playing this game anymore. That's just my opinion though, as maybe this is just not my kind of game.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game requires installing mods, mod managers, and community fixes to run properly or bypass technical limitations.

citations.review_text:
This is a game, that requires modding. And it just gets on my nerves even trying to ever enjoy this game.

I have owned the game since basically it came out. Even have the special edition. And even with it being 2026 and having all these editions and fixes ect. You STILL have to mod it to bypass the 60fps lock. That alone, makes it a complete write off to me. Because you will inevitably break something, or updates to your pc break something.

I spent 30 hours over the years modding the game, and never actually playing it. And thats just the hours I put INTO the game. Not on modding outside of it. And i just cant recommend a game that requires so much crap just to play.

This version still needs a bunch of fan-fixes to work properly. Tons of easy-to-fix bugs that you need mods to solve. So you install  a mod manager, script extender AND mods for those to work. Then you need another mod because of course they disable achievements just to make the game playable.

Pure Bethesda bs. 
Unplayable unless you want to spend more then an hour applying fan-made fixes. And even THEN some very egregious bugs persist. (Male characters using female grunts and vice versa) This for a 15-year old game's "special edition". Just embarrassing, downloading a pirated version that has all these fixes included is way less of a hassle. Do not buy.
other than being REQUIRED to mod for the game to even launch its a classic I played this gem back on the PS3 and playing on PC brings me back to when I was a child

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as basic, simplistic, or outdated compared to modern standards.

citations.review_text:
There are games I play, and then there are worlds I return to. Skyrim is the latter.

After more than 4,000 hours, I still find myself drawn back to its mountains, forests, winding roads, and familiar settlements. There is something remarkably peaceful about wandering through the wilderness with Jeremy Soule's soundtrack playing in the background, with no particular destination in mind.

What makes Skyrim exceptional is the freedom it gives me to inhabit its world on my own terms. I have created numerous characters over the years, each with their own backstory, personality, motivations, fighting style, and moral compass. Their stories extend well beyond the quests the game provides. Sometimes I am an adventurer seeking forgotten ruins. Sometimes I am a hunter wandering the wilderness. Sometimes I am simply a traveler looking for the next interesting place to explore.

Skyrim understands something that I think many modern open-world RPGs miss: the world itself can be the adventure. I don't always need an objective, a reward, or a cinematic event waiting around the next corner. Sometimes the journey is enough.

The modding community deserves tremendous credit for the game's longevity, but for me, mods are about enhancing an experience I already love rather than transforming it into something else.

Is Skyrim perfect? Far from it. The combat can be simplistic, the writing can be inconsistent, and its age is increasingly apparent. Yet I have played countless games with better graphics, more sophisticated combat, and more complex narratives. Very few have captured my imagination the way Skyrim has.

For me, the true measure of an RPG is not how compelling a story it tells me, but how compelling a story it allows me to tell.

Skyrim gives me that freedom.

And after thousands of hours, there is still something comforting about starting a new character, stepping into the world, and wondering where the road will take me this time.

One of my all-time favorites.  Replaying now it is showing its age:  combat, movement, graphics don't meet current standards for such open-world games, but it's still fun to play.  Lots to see and do.

What can I say, for a game its age it holds up. Helps that it has a loyal fanbase that virtually develops it for you thanks to the game's robust modding tools, you'll never run out of content really.

Combat is a bit basic, but as with anything Bethesda related its a click mod install away from improvement.
Honestly the only thing that can't really be fixed is the somewhat basic story, but I might just have high standards.

Goes on sale almost every couple months, you won't regret it. It's a bit of a Gamer right of passage to play, in the same league as half life and doom.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that quests can become locked or unfinishable due to bugs.

citations.review_text:
Overall 8/10

Pros: This game has some of the best
- Lore
- RPG elements (Classing, Builds, Playstyles, Races)
- Side content
- Replayability
- Vampirism if actually worth it now unlike in previous ES games
- Bugs (infinite items, duplicated weapons, wearing more pieces of armour than should be allowed etc)
- Quests can be completed at any level as the rewards are no longer scaled to your level (an issue Oblivion suffered from)
- DLC is very enjoyable
- Daedric quests

Cons:
- Bugs (The most bugged Bethesda game of them all, especially for bows). Many quests can become locked or unfinishable. 
- Lack of choice (Most quests dont have more than one ending)
- Smithing Skill (Might as well be called the difficulty slider skill with how detrimental this is to every build, your damage and armour become irrelevant if this is not levelled. Its annoying to level up so just use an item duplication glitch to infinitely smith jewellery). Such an unnecessary thing to put in the game and really ruins your level if levelled early.
- Thieves guild and dark brotherhood quests inferior to previous iterations.
- Ridiculous fetch quests that will be stuck in your journal the entire game.
- RNG for some quests can leave you playing for hours for diminishing returns.
- Soul Cairn (No explanation needed)

Skyrim is easily in my top 3 favorite games. The carefully crafted, enormous map is a delight; I've probably done 6 or 8 playthroughs over the years and find new things every time. Thee major quests (counting the main questline plus the faction quests here) are varied and substantial; your character has to make some hard choices that do affect other quests and gameplay. Crafting (enchanting, alchemy, smithing) provide ways to customize how you interact with the world as well as give you tools to modify the difficulty of the game (in addition to the difficulty setting, of course).

And yeah, there are some annoyances and bugs: some quests are fragile and can get stuck or bugged if you make certain choices; followers can be frustrating clumsy (*cough*floor traps*cough*) and the pathing isn't great; the physics can be hilarious ("why did that corpse fly half a kilometer?!"). But at this point, in 2026, all those things are quirky and a little funny, and I just save early and save often. This game is just pure comfort food now.

[b]tldr; Skyrim is 10/10, love it.[/b]
